messages:
anya: quick check — noticed a few CJS users getting `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` when installing the Node/TS SDK and bundling with Next/Vercel edge functions. stack: Next 13 edge runtime, Node 18, TS build target. anyone seen this pattern and a straightforward compatibility story?

sam: yup, common. usually comes down to package exports + dual build outputs. do we publish both .mjs and .cjs and set conditional exports? e.g.

sam: ```json
sam: {
sam:   "exports": {
sam:     ".": {
sam:       "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
sam:       "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
sam:     }
sam:   },
sam:   "type": "module"
sam: }
sam: ```

maria: +1. also ensure the package root doesn't force ESM-only by accident. Some bundlers (vite/next) will pick "import" entrypoints for ESM-only consumers which is fine, but CJS consumers with `require()` need the require path.

kyle: for Next edge specifically, remember that edge runtime uses Web APIs (Response, ReadableStream) and doesn't have full Node globals. If your SDK exposes a Node Readable stream in dist.cjs that confuses the edge bundler. Best is to ship a lightweight fetch-based runtime shim for edge.

anya: that helps. What about auth flow? a user tried to use process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY in an edge route and it was undefined at runtime on Vercel — any gotchas?

maria: edge functions on Vercel only get env vars exposed at build/deploy time if you mark them as runtime envs or use server-side only env injection. For client-side/edge, prefer a server-side route to sign requests or use platform secrets that the edge runtime exposes. Important: never ship the API key to the browser.

sam: one practical SDK change we did in the past: provide two entry modules — a node-friendly one that uses node-fetch/streams and an "edge-friendly" ESM entry that uses fetch + ReadableStream web API. Consumers can import via conditional exports: "browser"/"worker"/"node" fields. Example:

sam: ```json
sam: {
sam:   "exports": {
sam:     ".": {
sam:       "node": "./dist/node/index.cjs",
sam:       "import": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
sam:       "default": "./dist/edge/index.mjs"
sam:     }
sam:   }
sam: }
sam: ```

kyle: streaming quirks: Next edge streaming responses prefer web streams. If we offer streaming generation, ensure we expose a fetch-compatible streaming response (ReadableStream) rather than Node's stream.Readable. For server-side Node, keep the Node stream API.

anya: good point. Any recommendations for dev DX when testing locally? Next dev server sometimes masks runtime differences.

maria: use `VERCEL_ENV=preview` and test on a real edge deployment or use the edge-local runner. Also add unit tests that use a worker/edge-like polyfill (miniflare or worker-runtime) to catch issues earlier.

kyle: PR FYI: I opened a draft with conditional exports + edge entry + tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1298 — needs review and might fix the ERR_REQUIRE_ESM cases.

devex-bot: CI started for PR #1298 — linux, node 18, node 20, vite-test. Status: running.

anya: nice. for a quick patch we can also add docs snippet for CJS users: how to require dynamic import fallback. e.g.

anya: ```js
anya: // CJS-compatible import of an ESM-only package at runtime
anya: const { createRequire } = require('module');
anya: const requireFrom = createRequire(import.meta?.url || __filename);
anya: const sdk = requireFrom('./dist/index.cjs'); // or dynamic import fallback
anya: ```

sam: one more bundler note: Vite/ESBuild will sometimes inline polyfills and break edge. set `esbuild: { target: 'es2020' }` / keep builds minimal, and mark `sideEffects: false` in package.json to make tree-shaking less surprising.

maria: also add a short troubleshooting checklist to DEVEX docs:

maria: - verify package.exports has require/import paths
maria: - confirm edge vs node entrypoints
maria: - ensure streaming uses web streams for edge
maria: - avoid reading process.env in client/edge code; prefer server-side or platform secrets
maria: - run CI jobs against Node 18/20 + edge emulator

anya: perfect. I'll attach a minimal repro and link to the PR. @kyle can you add a small note in the CHANGELOG and ping me when CI passes?

kyle: will do, ping me in the PR thread.

devex-bot: CI passed for PR #1298 — all checks green :white_check_mark:

anya: thanks everyone — will close the loop after we publish a patch and update the devex doc.
